overview: Alodia, also known as Alwa, was a medieval Nubian kingdom centered at Soba on the Blue Nile. Archaeology reveals an important royal and religious city, but only a small portion has been examined.

items.text: Soba served as a royal, administrative and religious center. A Greek inscription records a king named David.
Excavations uncovered churches and buildings using stone, timber and both fired and unfired brick.
Distinctive Soba ware documents local pottery traditions. Investigators had not located its production workshops in the2019 report.
Written accounts describe visitors from the Mediterranean and Ethiopian highlands. The tenth-century traveler al-Aswani reported monasteries, gardens and a Muslim suburb.
Archaeology suggests decline by the thirteenth century. Later traditions place destruction in the early sixteenth; a visitor reported ruins in1523. These are different kinds of evidence.

sources.title: Drzewiecki and Ryndziewicz2019, Developing a New Approach to Research at Soba
sources.note: Checked passages and chronology qualifications appear in the accompanying evidence dossier.
